correctness.rationale: Laface--Ugaglia prove ampleness and \(\varepsilon(L;y)=2\sqrt5\) for the base class on a very general nine-point blow-up. For \(\delta=3H-\sum E_i\) and \(\alpha=E_1-E_2\), one has \(L\cdot\delta=4\), \(L\cdot\alpha=0\), and \(\alpha^2=-2\). The published Kac formula gives \(T_\alpha^m(L)=L+4m\alpha+4m^2\delta\), yielding the displayed coefficients and preserving primitivity and square \(20\). Totaro\'s Cremona-general-position argument shows that every finite Weyl word is realized on a very general nine-tuple and lifts, for surfaces, to an isomorphism of the corresponding blow-ups. A countable-intersection argument chooses one configuration for which all transformed configurations lie in the Laface--Ugaglia very-general locus, and then one common very general point for all pulled-back Seshadri equalities. The checker independently verifies the lattice action, inverse, coefficient formula, square and degree identities.

value.rationale: The initiating paper gives the first unconditional irrational one-point Seshadri constant on a very general nine-point plane blow-up. The accepted result shows this is not an isolated polarization or a scaling phenomenon: one fixed surface and one common very general point carry infinitely many primitive, pairwise distinct polarizations, all with the same fixed self-intersection \(20\) and the same maximal irrational constant \(2\sqrt5\), while their plane degrees are unbounded. Fixed volume and primitivity make the extension structural rather than a routine tensor-power family.
